sites.name: Fenway Park
sites.fact: Home of the Red Sox since 1912, the oldest ballpark in the major leagues. Its left-field wall, the Green Monster, is 37 feet high.
sites.hint: A ballpark tucked among the streets west of Back Bay.

sites.name: Massachusetts State House
sites.fact: Designed by Charles Bulfinch and completed in 1798. Paul Revere's company covered its dome in copper; it was first gilded in 1874.
sites.hint: The gold dome on Beacon Hill, above the Common.

sites.name: Boston Common
sites.fact: Set aside in 1634, it is the oldest public park in the United States. Cows grazed on it until 1830.
sites.hint: The open green in the middle of downtown, below the gold dome.

sites.name: USS Constitution
sites.fact: Launched in 1797 and nicknamed Old Ironsides in the War of 1812. It is the oldest commissioned warship still afloat in the world.
sites.hint: At the old navy yard in Charlestown, across the harbor from the North End.

sites.name: Bunker Hill Monument
sites.fact: A 221-foot granite obelisk, dedicated in 1843. It marks the battle of June 1775, which was fought mostly on Breed's Hill, where the monument stands.
sites.hint: The tall obelisk on the hill in Charlestown.

sites.name: Zakim Bridge
sites.fact: A cable-stayed bridge carrying ten lanes of highway over the Charles River. It opened in 2003 as part of the Big Dig.
sites.hint: The white cable fans over the river, north of downtown.

sites.name: Harvard Yard
sites.fact: Harvard was founded in 1636, which makes it the oldest college in the United States. The Yard is its original campus.
sites.hint: Red-brick buildings around a leafy yard in Cambridge, north of the river bend.

sites.name: MIT
sites.fact: MIT moved across the river from Boston in 1916. As pranks, students have put a police car and a fire truck on top of its Great Dome.
sites.hint: The domed campus on the Cambridge bank, across the river from Back Bay.

sites.name: Prudential Tower
sites.fact: Completed in 1964 and 228 metres tall. It was the tallest building in Boston until the Hancock Tower went up nearby in 1976.
sites.hint: The tall square tower in Back Bay, with an antenna on top.

sites.name: Logan Airport
sites.fact: Opened in 1923 and built out over the harbor on filled land. Planes land over the water, close to downtown.
sites.hint: The runways across the harbor from downtown, in East Boston.

sites.name: Old North Church
sites.fact: Built in 1723, the oldest church building standing in Boston. Two lanterns hung in its steeple on 18 April 1775 warned that British troops were coming by water.
sites.hint: The white steeple in the North End, near the harbor.

sites.name: Castle Island
sites.fact: A fort has stood here since 1634. Edgar Allan Poe served at Fort Independence as a young soldier in 1827.
sites.hint: The star-shaped granite fort at the tip of South Boston.
